newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia RAM downgrades Gopeng to A2.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia RAM downgrades Gopeng to A2.

text.p: The Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd (RAM) announced on Monday it has downgraded the long-term rating of Gopeng Bhd's 200 million ringgit bank guaranteed bonds to A2 from A1.
RAM said in a statement that the rating change reflected the structure of the bonds.

It said that the bonds were guaranteed by a consortium of banks, who were all rated by RAM. "It is RAM's policy that if the rating of a debt instrument is equal or higher than the rating of its guarantors, the former rating shall apply."
Some banks in the consortium were rated A2.

"The entire proceeds of Gopeng's bond issue were utilised to subscribe for the 200 million ringgit cumulative redeemable preference shares issued by its 45 percent-owned associate, Perak Hanjoong Simen Sdn Bhd," RAM said.
It said Perak Hanjoong, which is undergoing a restructuring exercise, has proposed a notes issuance facility of 450 million ringgit. The issue was being rated P2.
